_comment: Copy this file to launcher_config.json and fill in your own values. launcher_config.json is gitignored because it holds your OpenAI API key — never commit it. The books_py folder settings are optional: omit any of them to use the default shown here.

books_py._test_mode_comment: test_mode false processes every incoming image. Set it true to process only test_limit images (chosen at random) — useful for a cheap trial run.
books_py._retry_comment: Rate-limit backoff. If you hit the tokens-per-minute cap constantly, lower max_workers first — fewer parallel requests spend the budget slower. Images that still fail after retry_max_attempts stay in incoming_folder and are retried on the next run.
books_py._folders_comment: incoming_folder is scanned top level only, not recursively. sync_source_folder is scanned recursively first and new files are copied into incoming_folder. data_folder is where books_output.xlsx and the run CSVs live — keep it matching the other scripts.

storygraph._cooldown_comment: Both in days; 0 disables. skip_if_processed_within_days is the blanket guard so running the tool twice in a month doesn't redo the same work. retry_failed_after_days is how long a failed attempt waits before becoming eligible again. Books that were added, or were already on your shelf, are never reprocessed regardless of these.
storygraph._save_comment: How many books to process between spreadsheet saves. Saving rewrites every sheet and copies a backup, which on OneDrive takes longer than processing a book. Progress is always flushed at the end of a run, on interrupt and on error, so at most this many books' results are ever at risk. Set to 1 for the old save-after-every-book behaviour.
